events.title: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO less than two weeks after his exit, and the shares jumped more than 30%.
US stocks rebounded sharply Monday with the Nasdaq up about 7% midmorning, recovering much of last week's correction after Huang's return.
CoreWeave fell 12% on Nov 20 to $39.51, its lowest close in a year, as the S&P 500 dropped 3.7% and Oracle logged a seventh straight loss.
Tesla and SpaceX have each set up special board committees to explore a possible merger as Musk's AI spending grows.
Texas governor-elect Hinojosa called for a statewide data center moratorium as a state senator filed a bill to limit cooling methods and require water reporting.
Oracle said its roughly $300B OpenAI compute contract is fully funded after a $20B raise split between stock and debt, plus vendor financing.
Broadcom fell about 11% after analyst Ming-Chi Kuo said Google cut 2027 orders for Broadcom-designed TPU 8i chips by roughly 1 million units.
Walmart beat revenue forecasts at $188.8B with e-commerce up 17% and raised its yearly outlook for a third time, though US growth slowed.
Anthropic shares opened at $111.50 in their Nasdaq debut and closed at $97.17, up 17% from the $83 IPO price, valuing the company near $1.76T.
SpaceX completed a $32B debt sale backed by AI chips, with most of it priced at yields above 8%, high for an investment-grade borrower.
AMD fell 7.7% to about $489 after short seller Hunterbrook alleged its firmware kept reaching a blacklisted Chinese server maker; AMD disputed the claims.
Nvidia fell another 3.3% to about $146 as concerns over its CEO transition and tighter chip export rules outweighed strong quarterly results.
The Dow fell 1,101 points and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq each dropped over 2%, a sixth straight S&P loss, on AI spending doubts and Fed hike fears.
Salt Lake City approved a six-month pause on data centers to write energy and water rules after a $105M project applied for permits.
Jacksonville's city council took up a proposed one-year moratorium on large data center construction.
Initial jobless claims rose to 203,000 for the week to Nov 14, slightly above forecasts, with continuing claims at 1.76 million.
Musk said Tesla and SpaceX would probably be better together, as reports point to a possible merger announcement as soon as December.
Anthropic priced its upsized IPO at $83 a share, above its range, raising about $81.3B in the largest offering on record; ANT trades from Nov 19.
Nvidia closed 2.9% lower at about $151 despite beating forecasts, as CEO succession and China risk weighed; AMD rose 5.3% and Broadcom 3.7%.
Neocloud shares including CoreWeave and Iren fell alongside Nvidia after its results failed to lift sentiment.
Minutes of the Oct 27-28 meeting showed nearly all officials expect a quarter-point hike in December and a couple saw room for a larger move.
Target posted 5.6% comparable sales growth, its best in five years, raised its full-year sales outlook and its shares rose about 7%.
Lowe's beat profit forecasts with comparable sales up 1.8%, helped by about $250M of tariff refunds, and trimmed its margin outlook.
Fed Governor Waller said he backs a December hike and could support a half-point move if inflation keeps accelerating.
Nvidia clarified the limits on its future financing support for neocloud customers after Jensen Huang's exit raised doubts about its backstops.

nvidia.news: Nvidia fell about 23% in the week to Nov 20, its worst week since 2008, on CEO-succession and accounting worries despite a $115.8B quarter (Nov 17). On Nov 23 the board reinstated Jensen Huang and the shares jumped more than 30%.
cons: Accounting and governance questions not fully settled
nvidia.weak: Confidence hinges on governance, not demand: one more leadership or accounting shock would undo Monday's rebound.

labs.news: Anthropic's $81.3B IPO priced at $83 on Nov 18 and closed its first day at $97.17; OpenAI closed an $11B tranche at a $1.25T value (Nov 6), short of its $30B goal.

bigtech.news: All three major indexes closed in correction on Nov 20 after the Nasdaq lost about 10% in a week; Nov 23 brought a roughly 7% Nasdaq rebound on Huang's return. A reported Google cut to 2027 TPU orders (Nov 20) hints at capex discipline.

cloud.news: CoreWeave closed Nov 20 at $39.51, a one-year low, with its bonds near distressed levels, and Oracle fell a seventh straight day to $101.19. Oracle said on Nov 20 its OpenAI contract is fully funded after a $20B raise, and neoclouds rallied with Nvidia on Nov 23; HY spreads are 3.76%, up 0.49 pt in 30 days. Data-center counties in Dallas and Northern Virginia are 100% in drought.
pros: Oracle says OpenAI build fully funded (Nov 20)
cons: HY spread up 0.49 pt in 30 days
cloud.weak: Neocloud funding depends on open credit markets, which are tightening as spreads widen.

citizens.news: Household electricity prices are up 5.4% y/y and CPI energy 21% y/y, while lower-48 grid demand runs 1.4% above last year (PJM +1.4%, ERCOT +1.5%; SRP in Phoenix down 14% on mild weather). PJM's monitor warned Nov 13 of $5-10B more data-center costs on bills, Texas resumed data-center permits Nov 17, and Dallas County is 100% in severe drought; sentiment is 48 and the saving rate 3.8%.

spacex.news: Tesla and SpaceX each set up special committees to study a merger (reported Nov 22) after SpaceX's $32B chip-backed debt sale (Nov 19). Its Memphis Colossus site sits in a region where power costs keep rising (household electricity +5.4% y/y).

tesla.news: Tesla and SpaceX formed special committees to explore a merger (reported Nov 22), and FSD v15 is slated for wide release in December. Grid battery demand stays supported by electricity prices up 5.4% y/y.

consumer.news: Consumer sentiment is weak at 48 (down 5.6 points in a year) and imports from Vietnam rose 61% y/y in September, a key route for electronics. No major Apple-specific news this week.

retail.news: Walmart raised its outlook for a third time (Nov 19) and Target posted its best comps in five years (Nov 18); retail sales are up 6.8% y/y in October and e-commerce is 17.9% of sales.

autos.news: Light vehicle sales are flat at 16.0M annualized in October, used-car prices are down 3.3% y/y, and the 30-year mortgage at 7.28% signals high borrowing costs for car loans too.

fashion.news: Apparel prices are up 3.5% y/y in October and China imports up 34% y/y in September as tariffs were refunded to importers. No major brand news this week.

education.news: No notable news this week. Student loan balances were last reported at $1.78T.

banks.news: High-yield spreads widened 0.49 pt in 30 days to 3.76% and BBB to 1.22%, a one-year high, as AI data-center debt came under pressure; card delinquency is 2.85%, down from a year ago.

fed.news: The target range is 3.75-4.00% with fed funds at 3.88%, but core PCE is up 3.1% y/y, unemployment is 4.1% after 165K October jobs, and the Nov 18 minutes showed nearly all officials expect a December hike; the 30-year mortgage is 7.28%.

chips.news: Broadcom fell about 11% on Nov 20 after an analyst said Google cut 2027 TPU 8i orders by about a million units, and chip stocks slid on tighter export rules (Nov 19). Intel said Nov 18 it signed its first outside 18A-P customer.

power.news: PJM capacity prices are at the cap and its monitor warned Nov 13 of $5-10B more data-center costs; household electricity is up 5.4% y/y while Henry Hub gas is $3.10, near its 1-year average. Texas resumed data-center permits on Nov 17.

healthco.news: UnitedHealth fell about 4.7% on Nov 17 on Medicare Advantage worries; medical care CPI is up 1.9% y/y.

industrials.news: No notable industrial-specific news this week; demand for data-center generators and turbines stays strong while steel and aluminum tariffs keep costs high.

payments.news: No notable news this week. Card delinquency is 2.85%, slightly lower than a year ago, and holiday spending is forecast to grow about 4%.

trade.news: Imports from China (+34% y/y), Mexico (+40%) and Vietnam (+61%) all jumped in September after tariff refunds, while customs duties are down 17.5% y/y; the freight index is down 3% y/y.
